articles.title: Why We Might Be Missing Alien Signals: Stellar Weather Is Blurring the Message
articles.summary: The search for extraterrestrial intelligence has long focused on narrow radio signals. But new research shows that plasma turbulence around a star can spread those signals into a wider, fainter blur before they ever reach Earth. This could explain decades of radio silence.

articles.title: How a Disabled Parrot Fought His Way to the Top of the Pecking Order
articles.summary: Bruce, a kea with a missing upper beak, has become the dominant male in his aviary — the first disabled animal documented to achieve top rank without an ally. His secret? A unique jousting technique and a surprisingly low stress level.

articles.title: A Nanoscale Wrinkle Could Finally Make Superconductors Practical
articles.summary: Superconductors promise lossless electricity, but they're fragile — failing under heat or magnetic fields. By sculpting a substrate with atomic-scale ridges, researchers at Chalmers University induced superconductivity at higher temperatures and in strong magnetic fields, a crucial step toward real-world use.
